sources.entry: pyvips - A binding for libvips, a fast image processing library with low memory needs.

summary.one_liner: pyvips is a Python binding for the libvips image processing library, letting you build streaming, low-memory image pipelines from Python.
summary.what_it_does: It wraps libvips through cffi, building either a compiled API-mode extension or using ABI mode against the shared library. Programs describe a pipeline of image operations on a source image, and libvips executes the whole pipeline at once, streaming the image in sections from source to destination. The README says it passes the libvips test suite on Windows, macOS and Linux under CPython and PyPy3. It includes PEP 561 type stubs (pyvips/__init__.pyi) that can be regenerated when libvips operations change. A binary package (pyvips[binary]) bundles common libraries for pip install, and the Conda package ships a matching libvips.
use_cases: resize or shrink large images with low memory
batch convert or sharpen JPG and TIFF images
apply convolution filters to images in Python
process large whole-slide or tiff images in a streaming pipeline
notable: Streams image pipelines in parallel so entire images need not sit in memory
Uses cffi API mode when a C compiler and libvips headers are present, falling back to ABI mode otherwise
Ships PEP 561 type stubs with mypy support
Pre-built binary package via pip install pyvips[binary]
Benchmark claim in README: about 3x faster than ImageMagick and 5x less memory on one test
caveats: The pip binary package lacks some features such as PDF load and OpenSlide support
Requires libvips 8.2 or later, with 8.9 or later needed for all features
On Windows, DLL search paths must be set manually in code, and 64-bit Python is needed
ABI mode starts slower and is about 20% slower in execution
